findings.claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured; the change never reads them. When no SurrogateType is given, CreateContractlessMembers runs unconditionally. It ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract], [DataMember] and [IgnoreDataMember] on T and serializes every public read-write member under its CLR name. As a result, a member marked [IgnoreMember] (e.g. a secret) is still serialized. Custom string keys and int keys on T are also replaced by member names, so the wire format differs from what the dynamic resolver produces for the same type. The README and attribute docs describe this always-contractless behaviour, which contradicts the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests. The formatted type ProjectA.Keyed comes from a referenced assembly and is [MessagePackObject] with [IgnoreMember] Secret and [Key("custom_name")] Name. IgnoredMemberOfAttributedTypeIsNotSerialized fails on head because the generated source contains 'Secret'. StringKeyOfAttributedTypeIsHonoured fails on head because 'custom_name' is absent.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour over public members' means only public read-write instance properties and fields are serialized. Get-only properties and readonly fields are skipped, and deserialization always uses a parameterless constructor. This is what CreateContractlessMembers and IsPublicReadWrite implement.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour' means matching ContractlessStandardResolver. Public get-only properties and readonly fields are also serialized (IsReadable=true, IsWritable=false), and on deserialization they are set via a constructor whose parameters match by name. This requires CreateContractlessMembers to include public readable members, a constructor-matching step filling constructorParameters, and relaxing the parameterless-constructor requirement at GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:77.
